original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Five episodes have been dubbed into Australian language Yolŋu Matha for Naidoc Week, with Bandit voiced by a founding member of rock band King Stingray

It’s already been translated into 120 languages around the world but soon the globally loved children’s show Bluey will be available in an Australian Indigenous language for the first time.

Five episodes from seasons one and two have been dubbed into Yolŋu Matha, the Australian First Nations language of North-east Arnhem Land, as part of an initiative for National Aboriginal and Islanders Day Observance Committee (Naidoc) Week.

Due to be broadcast and streamed for the first time on Sunday 5 July, episodes The Beach, The Creek, Sleepytime, Grandad and Rug Island have been re-voiced by Dimathaya Burrawanga from the band King Stingray (as Bandit), Yolŋu educator and translator Rosie Mununggurr (as Chilli) and Andrew Gurruwiwi as the granddad.

The children voicing Bluey and Bingo, who haven’t been named to protect their privacy, are local children from North-east Arnhem Land.

The project was developed with Yolŋu Radio and the Aboriginal Resource and Development Services (ARDS), in collaboration with Bluey creators Ludo Studio and the ABC. Kelly Williams, the ABC’s director of First Nations strategy, said the Indigenous language episodes will “bring the North-east Arnhem Land language and culture into homes across the country”.

“To hear these stories told in Yolŋu Matha, languages spoken on this continent for thousands of generations, is incredibly special,” said Julia Wormer and Sylvia Nulpinditj, co-chief executive officers at ARDS. “We hope this project contributes to a future where First Nations languages are increasingly heard, celebrated and recognised as a vital part of Australia’s story.”

Bluey, Bingo, Bandit and Chilli have been streamed into millions of homes since the show launched in 2018. It is available in more than 140 countries and the animated series has topped the US streaming charts for the past two years.

Naidoc Week runs from 5 to 12 July. Its theme is 50 Years of Deadly, honouring the strength, leadership and resilience of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and communities.

The Indigenous language episodes of Bluey will also be screened at this year’s Garma festival in August.

---

[Lähde: ABC (Australian Broadcasting Corporation)]
The ABC today announced a major Indigenous language initiative for NAIDOC Week, bringing Australia’s most loved blue heeler family to audiences in Yolŋu Matha, the First Nations language of Northeast Arnhem Land.

The project, led by Yolŋu Radio and the Aboriginal Resource and Development Services (ARDS), has been developed in collaboration with the ABC and Bluey producers Ludo Studio.

Five Bluey episodes have been translated, The Beach, The Creek, Sleepytime, Grandad and Rug Island, selected for their culturally relevant themes of family and country.

The Indigenous language Bluey episodes will launch on ABC iview on Sunday 5 July and will also feature on the big screen at the Garma Festival in August.

The episodes were produced at Yolŋu Radio’s studio in Northeast Arnhem Land, with Bandit voiced by Dimathaya Burrawanga, founding member of Yolŋu surf rock band King Stingray, and Chilli by Rosie Mununggurr.

The Bluey Indigenous language initiative is a centrepiece of the ABC’s NAIDOC Week 2026 programming, celebrating Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander cultures, creative voices and languages across screen, audio and digital platforms.

ABC Director, First Nations Strategy Kelly Williams: “Bluey has become part of family life for many Australians, so hearing these stories told in Yolŋu Matha is a powerful way of bringing Northeast Arnhem Land language and culture into homes across the country.  At the ABC, we’re committed to ensuring Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander languages are part of the national conversation and these episodes, alongside our broader NAIDOC Week content, is a strong example of that commitment in action.”

ARDS co-chief executive officers Julia Wormer and Sylvia Nulpinditj: “Bluey has become a shared language for families right across Australia, so to hear these stories told in Yolŋu Matha, languages spoken on this continent for thousands of generations, is incredibly special. payload.title: Bluey saa ensimmäisen version Australian alkuperäiskielellä
payload.summary: Lastensarja Blueysta julkaistaan viisi Yolŋu Matha -kielelle dubattua jaksoa osana Australian NAIDOC-viikon ohjelmistoa.
payload.content:
Suosittu australialainen lastenohjelma Bluey tulee ensimmäistä kertaa saataville Australian alkuperäiskielellä, kun viisi sarjan ensimmäisen ja toisen kauden jaksoa on dubattu Yolŋu Matha -kielelle NAIDOC-viikkoa varten. Kyseessä on Koillis-Arnheminmaan First Nations -kieli, ja hanke kuuluu ABC:n vuoden 2026 NAIDOC-viikon ohjelmistoon.

## Viisi jaksoa Yolŋu Matha -kielellä

Bluey on jo käännetty noin 120 kielelle eri puolilla maailmaa. Yolŋu Matha -versio on kuitenkin sarjalle ensimmäinen Australian alkuperäiskielellä tehty versio. Dubatut jaksot ovat peräisin sarjan ensimmäiseltä ja toiselta kaudelta.

Yolŋu Matha on Koillis-Arnheminmaalla puhuttu Australian First Nations -kieli. Uusi kieliversio on tehty osana National Aboriginal and Islanders Day Observance Committee -viikkoa, joka tunnetaan lyhenteellä NAIDOC. Viikon ohjelmistossa nostetaan esiin aboriginaalien ja Torresinsalmen saarten kansojen kulttuureja, luovia ääniä ja kieliä.

## Äänitykset tehtiin Koillis-Arnheminmaalla

Jaksot tuotettiin Yolŋu Radion studiossa Koillis-Arnheminmaalla. Blueyn isän Banditin äänenä kuullaan Dimathaya Burrawangaa, joka on Yolŋu surf rock -yhtye King Stingrayn perustajajäsen. Blueyn äidin Chillin äänenä on Rosie Mununggurr.

Tuotantopaikka ja ääninäyttelijät kytkevät hankkeen samaan alueeseen, jonka kielellä jaksot on toteutettu. Lähdeaineisto vahvistaa jaksojen määrän, kieliversion, studion sekä Banditin ja Chillin ääninäyttelijät, mutta ei nimeä yksittäisiä jaksoja.

## Osa ABC:n NAIDOC-ohjelmistoa

Yolŋu Matha -dubbaus on ABC:n NAIDOC Week 2026 -ohjelmiston keskeisiä osia. Ohjelmakokonaisuus juhlistaa aboriginaalien ja Torresinsalmen saarten kansojen kulttuureja, luovia tekijöitä ja kieliä televisiossa, radiossa, äänisisällöissä ja digitaalisilla alustoilla.

Hankkeen merkitys liittyy erityisesti kieleen ja näkyvyyteen: kansainvälisesti laajalle levinnyt lastenohjelma julkaistaan nyt myös Australian alkuperäiskielellä. Lähteissä ei kerrota tarkkoja lähetysaikoja, mutta ne vahvistavat, että viiden jakson Yolŋu Matha -versio on osa vuoden 2026 NAIDOC-viikon ohjelmaa.
